title: Federated Shadowing & Privacy-Bounded Probe Synthesis Playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines a repeatable, privacy-bounded approach for running federated shadowing across Redwood’s Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments and for synthesizing probes that approximate tenant workloads without leaking sensitive data. It codifies safe sampling, local privacy transformations, orchestration patterns, monitoring contracts, and regression triage tie-ins. Use this playbook when a model or serving change requires cross-environment validation with tenant-level privacy guarantees.

Why this exists
---------------
- Many production issues only surface when the combination of client prompts, KV cache state, and quantization interact in a target environment.
- Full traffic mirroring is often disallowed by privacy or legal constraints. Federated shadowing aims to provide coverage with provable privacy limits and bounded telemetry while preserving fidelity for regression detection.

Scope and applicability
-----------------------
- Applies to: eval-mesh shadowing (on-hosted eval mesh), Dedicated clusters, and Private deployments where local privacy controls are required.
- Not for: investigative human review of raw customer PII; do not use this playbook when retention or data export rules would be violated.
- Primary owners: Applied ML (probe-fabricator), Eval Orchestration (shadow-orch), and Privacy & Compliance.

Definitions
-----------
- Federated Shadowing: orchestrated execution of synthesized or sampled probes across multiple deployment tiers (hosted/dedicated/private) under a shared evaluation contract.
- Probe Synthesis: programmatic generation of evaluation inputs derived from anonymized telemetry anchors and service schemas.
- Privacy Budget (ε): target local differential privacy epsilon assigned to a probe population or tenant slice.
- Fidelity Score: automated metric comparing probe responses to baseline reference (range 0-1).

Preconditions (must satisfy before starting)
-------------------------------------------
1) Legal & Data: a signed data-handling attestation for the target tenant class and confirmation from Privacy & Compliance that federated shadowing is permitted for the planned probe class.
2) Infrastructure: shadow-orch and evaluator-sidecar deployed to the target Dedicated/Private clusters.
3) Observability: redwood-console route and a telemetry pipeline path created (trace, per-probe metadata, fidelity metric ingestion).
4) Baseline: reference model artifact and golden probe-set stored in eval-asset-registry with hash and version.

High-level procedure
--------------------
1. Define objective and success criteria
   - Example objectives: detect regression in function-call accuracy for payments flow; measure latency shift under quantized kernels.
   - Success criteria: fidelity_score_drop <= 0.05; tail latency 99th <= baseline*1.2; privacy budget per-tenant ε <= 2.0.
2. Curate anchor set and synthesis rules
   - Select anchors: telemetry-derived canonical prompts (no PII).
   - Synthesis rules: template expansion, slot fuzzing, constrained slot distributions to mimic real context lengths.
3. Assign privacy transforms and sampling budgets
   - Apply local differential privacy noise where text-derived anchors may contain reidentification risk.
   - Sampling ratio guidance: default 1% of traffic per tenant for heavy-tenants, min 0.05% for long-tail tenants; absolute cap 5% per-tenant.
4. Fabricate probe manifest and schedule federated runs
   - Create probe manifest (see example below).
   - Use shadow-orch to schedule shadow runs across eval-mesh slots in Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.
5. Run minicanary then scaled federated pass
   - Minicanary (N=100–1k probes) for smoke checks.
   - If minicanary passes (fidelity and latency within thresholds), scale to planned budget.
6. Monitor live metrics and enforce privacy controls
   - Real-time telemetry must include per-probe hash, fidelity score, sampling seed, and privacy-epsilon used.
   - Telemetry retention: aggregated metrics 90d, raw probe inputs and outputs 30d in secure escrow, then auto-delete.
7. Triage regressions and roll decisions
   - If fidelity drop > threshold or functional errors detected, follow regression triage matrix (see section).

Probe manifest example (JSON as string)
--------------------------------------
Use this as an example in eval-mesh. Operators should redact any PII.

{"probe_id":"pf-2027-001", "service":"orders-api", "slice":"checkout-payment", "sample_ratio":"0.01", "privacy_epsilon":"1.5", "synthesis_profile":"schema-anchored", "ttl":"72h", "owner":"applied-ml/probe-fabricator"}

Probe synthesis rules (concise)
-----------------------------
- Anchors must be one-way hashed before storage (SHA-256 with key salt).
- Replace candidate entities with synthetic tokens drawn from a service-specific lexicon (e.g., <AMOUNT>, <CARD_TYPE>).
- Use constrained slot distributions to preserve context-length histograms.
- For function-call probes, synthesize arguments within valid schema ranges.

Sampling and budget table
-------------------------
| Config key               | Recommended default | Hard limit |
|--------------------------|---------------------|------------|
| per-tenant sample_ratio  | 0.01 (1%)           | 0.05 (5%)  |
| min_sample_ratio         | 0.0005 (0.05%)      | 0.001 (0.1%) |
| privacy_epsilon (ε)      | 1.0                 | 2.0        |
| probe_ttl                | 72h                 | 168h (7d)  |
| raw_probe_retention      | 30d (secure escrow) | 90d (restricted) |\nTelemetry and monitoring contract
----------------------------------
- Metrics emitted per-probe: probe_id, service, slice, fidelity_score, baseline_hash, latency_ms, kernel_variant, quant_profile, sampling_seed, privacy_epsilon.
- Alerting rules (examples):
  - fidelity_score_drop_alert: fires when rolling 1-hour fidelity drops > 0.05 and sustained 15 minutes. Severity: P2. Pager: Applied ML oncall.
  - quant-fallback-spike: fires if >2% of probes triggered quant_fallback policy in 10m window. Severity: P3.
  - tail-latency-regression: 99th latency > baseline * 1.25 for 5m. Severity: P1.

Privacy controls and enforcement
--------------------------------
- Local transforms executed by evaluator-sidecar before probe payload leaves tenant boundary in Private deployments.
- Privacy ledger: every federated run must register a privacy transaction with the privacy service recording cumulative ε per-tenant per-day.
- If cumulative ε for any tenant exceeds the configured daily cap (default 2.0), the shadow-orch must throttle new probes for that tenant.

Runbook: step-by-step (operator)
--------------------------------
1. Prepare: confirm probe manifest stored at eval-asset-registry and legal attestation present.
2. Smoke minicanary: rw-shadow run --manifest pf-2027-001 --mode minicanary --env hosted
3. Validate telemetry: confirm telemetry pipeline receives fidelity scores and privacy_epsilon tags.
4. Scale: rw-shadow run --manifest pf-2027-001 --mode federated --env hosted,dedicated,private --budget 10000
5. Watch alerts for first 30 minutes; if P1/P2 triggers, pause orchestration: rw-shadow pause --run <run_id>
6. Post-run: generate a run report with fidelity deltas and privacy ledger entry and store under eval-asset-registry/report/<run_id>.

Regression triage matrix (short)
--------------------------------
- Severity P1 (block rollout): fidelity_drop >= 0.15 OR functional errors in >0.5% probes OR 99th latency > baseline*1.5. Immediate rollback.
- Severity P2 (investigate within 2 hours): fidelity_drop between 0.05 and 0.15 OR quant_fallback spike 1–2%. Follow automated bisect and notify Applied ML.
- Severity P3 (monitor): small fidelity drift <0.05 or isolated errors. Create ticket, schedule probe augmentation.

Automated follow-ups and tooling integration
--------------------------------------------
- Auto-bisect: on P2, shadow-orch forks a binary bisect across kernel/quant variants using the run’s probe cohort. Results linked to the run report.
- Probe re-synthesis: if drift correlates to a slice, the probe-fabricator will generate targeted adversarial probes and tag them with ‘repro-ask’ for human review.
- Eval change request: create a PR in eval-asset-registry pointing to the manifest and include run report and recommended action.

Operational knobs and safe defaults
----------------------------------
- Default run concurrency: 200 probes/sec per eval-mesh slot.
- Default fidelity acceptance: mean >= 0.92 and 95th quantile fidelity >= 0.85.
- Default privacy daily cap per-tenant: ε_daily <= 2.0.

Examples: common scenarios
-------------------------
1) Quant migration verification (Dedicated): small sample_ratio (0.5%) across candidate quant profiles; run minicanary against warm cache state; expect median latency drop and fidelity change < 0.03.
2) Function-call regression detection (Private): synthesize function-call probes derived from schema; privacy_epsilon 0.5; run federated small-batch; check function-arg parsing accuracy.
3) Multi-tenant tail search (Hosted): sample long-context tenants at min_sample_ratio with TTL 168h to assemble long-tail anchor registry for next synth iteration.

Postmortem & knowledge capture
------------------------------
- Required artifacts after any P1: run report, privacy ledger dump for affected tenants, bisect output, and reproduction kit (subset of synthesized probes).
- Store findings in eval-harness/retrospectives with tags: "federated-shadowing", "postmortem".

Safety checklist (pre-run)
-------------------------
- [ ] Legal clearance obtained
- [ ] Privacy ledger initialized and cap configured
- [ ] Probe manifest hashed and stored in eval-asset-registry
- [ ] Evaluator-sidecar privacy transforms validated
- [ ] Observability endpoints and alerts configured
